topic: The People's Health c1250 to Present
subject: history

items.q: Did medieval people know germs cause disease?
items.correct: No — germ theory came later (Pasteur, 1861); they blamed the Four Humours, miasma and God.
items.why: Ideas about disease changed slowly; bacteria weren't linked to illness until the 19th century.

items.q: Has medical progress always been steady and continuous?
items.correct: No — there were long periods of stagnation and even regression.
items.misconception: Yes, it improved at a constant rate.
items.random_wrong: There was no progress until the year 2000.
items.why: For example, Roman public-health knowledge was largely lost in the early Middle Ages.

items.q: Did one person single-handedly create modern medicine?
items.correct: No — progress relied on many people, teams and wider factors (war, government, technology).
items.misconception: Yes, one scientist did it alone.
items.random_wrong: Medicine was perfected by the Romans.
items.why: Breakthroughs build on others' work and on social and technological change.
